key_insight: BenchX shows that cancer-detection AI can look strong overall but still fail badly in underrepresented subgroups, tumor sizes, and imaging protocols.
clinical_relevance: This benchmark highlights the need to test medical AI beyond average accuracy so clinicians and developers can identify where performance may be unreliable in real-world use.
method: Built an open benchmark of 85,355 CT scans.
Evaluated 12 tumor-detection AI models across tumor size, location, patient subgroup, and imaging protocol.
Used LLMs to extract and structure subgroup information from clinical data for scalable analysis.
evidence_signal: The benchmark systematically assessed 12 models on 85,355 CT scans and found poorer performance in rare or underrepresented groups, including young, female African Americans.
watch_item: Subgroup findings are only as strong as the quality and completeness of the underlying clinical labels and may not cover every tumor type or deployment setting.
paper_title: BenchX: Benchmarking AI Models for Cancer Detection and Localization with Demographic and Protocol Biases
